name: opencode-focus
description: Status-aware terminal titles, minimal desktop notifications and click-to-focus window for the opencode TUI (GNOME/Wayland support).

installation.summary: Install from npm: `opencode plugin opencode-focus --global` (server + TUI).
installation.markdown:
## Installation

### Plugins (server + TUI)
```bash
opencode plugin opencode-focus --global
```

This installs two plugins:
- **server** — desktop notifications via `notify-send` (error, waiting decision, completion once per session, retry)
- **TUI** — window title with state (spinner/status) and the waiting-decision notification

Restart opencode to load.

### GNOME extension (optional, recommended)
Enables focus-based notification suppression and click-to-focus:
```bash
npx opencode-focus setup
```
Log out/in so GNOME Shell discovers the extension, then validate:
```bash
npx opencode-focus status
```

Without the extension the plugins still work — they just always notify (no focus suppression).

usage.markdown:
## Usage

### Window title states
| State | Title |
|---|---|
| Generating | `⠋ <title>` or `⠇ <title> · ▶ <step>` |
| Waiting for you | `◉ <title> · ⏸ waiting permission` (or `answer`) |
| Done | `✓ <title>` |
| Error | `✗ <title>` |

### Notifications
- **Focus suppresses**: with the GNOME extension active, no notification is sent when the terminal already has focus
- **Dedupe**: completion 1x per session; errors 1x per message
- **Click-to-focus**: each notification has a "Focus terminal" action

### Diagnostics
```bash
tail -f ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode-focus.log
```

### Duplicate protection
The TUI plugin uses a shared KV lock (`opencode_focus_title_owner`) — only the first loaded instance writes the window title, even if an old local copy is also installed.
